solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sea creatures in this Walpole novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Marine animals appear in a novel by the writer Walpole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun (a book by Walpole) but works as an adjective, 'new', signalling the anagram of THIS WALPOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: These large dolphins are marine mammals, so they are fairly called creatures of the sea.

clue.text: Sees lap dancing gives enjoyment

indicators.note: letters dancing about move into a fresh order, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watching a lap dance finds it enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them pleasure, so the verb in the third person matches the phrase.

clue.text: Stone circles around Flint's centre

indicators.note: around tells us the circuits go round the outside of the single letter

parts.note: circles, as runs round a track, are laps

indicators.note: centre of a five-letter word picks out its middle letter

explanation.surface: A stone ring is arranged around the middle of a piece of flint.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis lazuli is a blue semi-precious stone, often shortened to its first word.

clue.text: Awful threat, closure of the Crucible, perhaps

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are put in a new order
closure of means the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A dreadful threat leads to the shutting of a venue called the Crucible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible is a theatre in Sheffield, famous for hosting the world snooker championship; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crucible is an example of a playhouse, which the 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: One entertaining those at sea on steamship

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first part sits on top of the second
at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone entertains the passengers aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess is a woman who entertains guests, so she is one doing the entertaining.

clue.text: Investigates skin disorder in old lackey, retired

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters go inside the reversed piece
retired means drawn back, so the old lackey is read backwards

parts.note: a lackey, someone used by others, is a tool

indicators.note: disorder says the letters of the word skin are jumbled

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a skin complaint suffered by a former servant now pensioned off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like part of a medical phrase but is the anagram signal; 'retired' turns the old lackey round, and 'in' puts the scrambled letters inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: To look into a matter is an idiom for examining or researching it closely.

clue.text: Well up about care of cat

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to well up is to rise suddenly, to surge
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: A carer gets emotional while looking after a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is short for cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not the pet the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip, and the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip with knotted cords.

clue.text: High, the Parisian church tower with spire

parts.note: a high price is a steep one
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A tall French church tower topped with a spire.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tower of a church together with its tapering spire.

clue.text: Counterfeit pounds — beats money!

indicators.note: counterfeit means faked, so the letters of pounds are reworked

parts.note: to lick someone is to beat them, so beats gives licks

explanation.surface: Forged pound notes are the best way to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats' reads as a verb meaning 'outdoes' but supplies LICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spondulicks is a jokey slang word for cash.

clue.text: Put on an act if performance cancelled

parts.note: a performance is a show
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: Someone pretends when a performance is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off is to behave in a showy way to impress, putting on an act.

clue.text: Intended to help race officials, to begin with

parts.note: something meant for a person is intended to help them
starters are the officials who start races

explanation.surface: Something meant to assist the officials of a race, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: For starters is an idiom meaning firstly or as a first point.

clue.text: Drop of ouzo when one's in watering hole

indicators.note: a drop of a drink is its smallest part, here the first letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
one is the numeral I and 's stands for is, giving I S

explanation.surface: A small amount of ouzo is drunk when someone is in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a desert spot with water, a literal watering hole.

clue.text: Club official, someone much valued at end of year

parts.note: a person much prized is called a treasure

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A club member highly prized at the close of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer keeps the funds of a club or society, an elected official role.

clue.text: Be worthy of extremely durable present

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the outermost letters of durable

parts.note: to present food is to serve it

explanation.surface: A long-lasting gift that is worth having.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, to have earned it.

clue.text: A good example to follow part way on line

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
a way of doing things is a mode

explanation.surface: A good example is partly found along a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person others look up to and imitate.

clue.text: Film-maker in governing body, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means a word that sounds like the piece is wanted

parts.note: a senate is a governing or legislative body

explanation.surface: A movie director sits in a legislature, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: Mack Sennett was an American silent-film producer, creator of the Keystone Kops.
explanation.definitionFit: Sennett produced and directed hundreds of silent comedies, a famous maker of films.

clue.text: One close to wicketkeeper having edge on members

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first piece comes after the one it is on

parts.note: legs are limbs, also called members
the lip of a cup is its edge

explanation.surface: A fielder stands near the keeper with an advantage over the team members.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg slip is a fielding position just behind the batsman on the leg side, close to the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg slip is a fielding position, and the player there stands near the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: One picking up rest in country many ignored

indicators.note: in places the resting piece inside what is left of the country
ignored means left out, so many is dropped from the country

parts.note: Germany is a country
to lean is to rest against something

explanation.surface: A person collecting what remains in a nation largely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' leaves GER of the country once the many is dropped; 'in' then wraps those letters round the word for rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner picks up leftover grain after harvest, or gathers facts bit by bit.

clue.text: Peer got embarrassed in ward

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests being thrown into confusion, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A nobleman blushed while in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ward' suggests a hospital, but means a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A protégé is someone guided and protected by a patron, like a ward by a guardian.

clue.text: Metro users, some characters in pocket

indicators.note: some characters in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Commuters on the underground, some of them odd types, pocketing things.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is slang for pocketing it, often dishonestly.

clue.text: Unusual trade-in worked out

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A strange part-exchange deal was arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has trained has exercised or worked out, as at a gym.

clue.text: The Spanish tucked into winter cabbage and sausage

indicators.note: tucked into says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: the savoy is a crinkly cabbage grown for winter
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spanish diners eat cabbage with sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but means placing inside. A saveloy is a spicy British smoked sausage, often sold in chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a seasoned red sausage, usually bought cooked.

clue.text: A comrade's mixed a fizzy drink

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend's cocktail is mixed with a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'comrade's' counts as fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soda is a sweet vanilla-flavoured carbonated soft drink.

clue.text: Film one in advance

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for advance

parts.note: to advance is to move forward
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A film is screened before release.
explanation.definitionFit: Movie is the everyday word for a film.

clue.text: Little-known part of domino rules

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some obscure points in the rules of dominoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor figure is not well known, of lesser importance.

clue.text: Study is over: that is, indefinitely adjourned

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the study and is are read backwards together

parts.note: a den is a private study
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: The study session ends, that is, it is put off without a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for without a day, used of a meeting adjourned with no date to resume.

clue.text: Completely perplex small number on bonus

parts.note: n is used for an unspecified number, here a small one
a plus is an extra advantage or bonus

explanation.surface: A tiny figure tacked onto a bonus completely baffles someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is fodder, not a positional link.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to bewilder them so they do not know how to react.

clue.text: Wave bowler hat in US skating race

parts.note: a roller is a long sea wave
Americans call a bowler hat a derby

explanation.surface: Someone waves a bowler hat at an American skating contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Roller derby is a contact sport on roller skates in which team members race around an oval track.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller derby is a race-style contest between teams on roller skates.
